question: A radiologist performs an ultrasound at 18 weeks gestation and, at the request of the pregnant woman and her husband, informs them that the foetus is female. Under the PC&PNDT Act 1994, which statement is correct?

answers.text: No offence is committed because the information was requested by the pregnant woman, who has a right to know.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The pregnant woman's request does not create a right to disclosure of the foetal sex, nor does it absolve the doctor. Both the requesting party and the communicating doctor commit an offence under the PC&PNDT Act. The Act is designed to prevent sex-selective abortions and the prohibition is absolute.

answers.text: The radiologist has committed an offence under the PC&PNDT Act by communicating the sex of the foetus.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Section 5 and 6 of the PC&PNDT Act 1994 prohibit determination and communication of the sex of the foetus. The radiologist commits an offence regardless of who requested the information or the method used. Punishment includes imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; the radiologist's registration may also be suspended.

answers.text: An offence is committed only if a sex-selective abortion is subsequently performed.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The offence under PC&PNDT is the communication of foetal sex itself — it is not contingent on whether a subsequent abortion occurs. The Act targets the chain of sex selection at the diagnostic stage to prevent selective abortion.

answers.text: The Act only applies if pre-conception sex selection techniques are used — post-conception sex disclosure is not covered.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Act covers both pre-conception and pre-natal diagnostic techniques. 'Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques' explicitly include ultrasound used to disclose foetal sex after conception. Post-conception sex disclosure is a primary target of the Act.

overallFeedback.feedback: Under PC&PNDT: communicating foetal sex = offence, full stop. No exception for patient request, no requirement for subsequent abortion to occur, applies to post-conception ultrasound disclosure.
Correct. Communicating foetal sex is an offence regardless of the reason or by whom it was requested. The PC&PNDT Act is strict-liability in nature for this disclosure.
